assumptions: The rate card provided is a PLACEHOLDER: all 24 backlog tasks are costed against a single generic 'Team member' role at $75/hr with 1 FTE available, because no real team members, specialised roles (e.g. Frontend/Backend/QA/DevOps), or individual hourly rates have been assigned yet. These costs are INDICATIVE ONLY and must be re-estimated once real roles and rates are set.

1 FTE at 1 person cannot realistically deliver ~2,360 hours of work solo in a normal timeframe (that's roughly 1.4 person-years of work for one person); this estimate assumes the hours will actually be delivered by a team of equivalent size/skill once properly staffed, or that the single FTE works across an extended multi-year timeline. This is flagged as a significant staffing risk.

Story points were converted to engineering hours using a rough heuristic of ~8-9 hours per point, adjusted upward for tasks with known high complexity/risk (payment integration, legacy migration, multi-currency, RBAC) and downward for simpler UI/config tasks.
No historical actuals (real spend data) are available for this project yet; this estimate is based purely on backlog scope and story points, not on observed team velocity or past delivery costs.

Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for Stripe/PCI review, legacy Oracle migration tooling, staging/CI cloud infrastructure, and a general contingency for third-party/legacy unknowns; actual vendor quotes have not been obtained.

PW-8 (Legacy data migration, 21 points) and PW-7 (Payment provider integration, 13 points) are assumed to carry extra risk premiums baked into their hour allocations due to data volume (2M+ invoice lines) and financial/webhook reconciliation complexity.
Scenario spread (Optimistic -12.8%, Pessimistic +19.3%) reflects uncertainty due to the placeholder team/rate structure and lack of historical velocity data, not confidence in scope estimates alone.
Priority breakdown totals are derived by allocating each task's estimated labour cost (plus a proportional share of non-labour costs) according to its priority label (Urgent/High/Medium/Low).
input.reasoning: Backlog totals 24 tasks / 201 story points. Hours were derived per task using ~8-9 hours/point as a baseline, with premiums added for high-risk items (payment integration, legacy migration, RBAC, multi-currency, 2FA) and slight reductions for simpler tasks (contract tests, decommissioning, ticket submission). This produced a total of ~2,360 engineering hours, costed at the single placeholder rate of $75/hr = $177,000 labour. Non-labour costs of $10,000 cover indicative third-party/infrastructure spend (Stripe/PCI review, Oracle migration tooling, CI/staging cloud costs, and a general contingency buffer for unknowns in legacy integration). Total Most Likely estimate: $187,000. Optimistic (-13%) and Pessimistic (+19%) scenarios reflect uncertainty from the placeholder rate card, single-FTE staffing constraint, and absence of historical velocity data. Priority breakdown allocates cost proportionally by task priority label to show where budget is concentrated (Urgent items like auth and payments are relatively cheap in point-count but critical path; Medium-priority items dominate due to sheer number of tasks).

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff, Low priority, 13 points) to a later phase; support staff can use direct DB/admin tooling short-term.
reductions.effect: Removes ~130 hours of build time from the initial release scope.

reductions.description: Defer PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting, Low priority, 8 points) and PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API, Low priority, 5 points) to a post-launch phase since neither blocks core customer-facing functionality.
reductions.effect: Removes ~116 hours of build time; contract tests can be added once helpdesk integration stabilises.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of PW-14 (Multi-currency support) at launch to a single settlement currency (USD) with display-only conversion for EUR/PLN, deferring full multi-currency settlement.
reductions.effect: Cuts estimated hours on PW-14 roughly in half by removing settlement/reconciliation logic for non-USD currencies initially.

reductions.description: Defer PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal, Low priority) until after the new portal has been live and stable for a full billing cycle, rather than in the initial delivery window.
reductions.effect: Removes ~60 hours from the initial estimate; legacy infra costs continue slightly longer but reduce delivery risk.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour contingency line from $3,500 to $1,500 once real vendor quotes for Oracle migration tooling and Stripe/PCI review are obtained, replacing guesswork with actuals.
reductions.effect: Lowers non-labour budget; requires follow-up procurement step before committing.
